feature: Titles play a soft whoosh and tick as they build
summary: A title can now be heard arriving: one Sounds switch in its Title section lays a bar of sound under it, a soft whoosh as the words come in and a light tick as a small accent lands. The bar moves, trims, copies and deletes with the title, plays, and goes into the exported MP4.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: title-sounds-whoosh-and-tick-walk.

try.do: Open a recording, open the Library, and double click Editorial Serif to put it in.
Click the title on the canvas and find Sounds in the Title section, under Background. It is off.
Click the Sounds switch on. A Title Sounds bar appears under the title on its own audio track.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Home, then Space, and listen: a whoosh as the headline rises, a tick as the rule under it draws on.
Drag the title's bar along the timeline, then drag its right edge shorter. The sound bar follows both.
Set Energy to Punchy and play it again: a shorter, brighter whoosh.
Choose File > Export…, pick MP4, and play the file: the sounds are in it.
Click Sounds off. The bar goes.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: Is the whoosh soft enough to sit under your own voice and still be noticed?
Does the tick land where your eye sees the accent arrive, not after it?
Is one Title Sounds bar on its own track what you expect, or would you rather the sounds sat inside the title's own bar?
Should Sounds stay a switch in the Title section, or would you also want it on the title's right-click menu?
Do you want a choice of sound sets (softer, clickier) or is one set, shaped by Energy, enough?
rough: No mock covers title sounds, so the Sounds row is placed by the placement contract (the placement contract table at the top of UX-PATTERNS: the panel holds values you set) as a plain switch row like the caption Shadow switch.
While a title's bar is being dragged, its sound bar stays put and catches up the moment you let go.
Dragging the Title Sounds bar on its own snaps it back under its title: it is linked. To move it freely you would turn Sounds off and add a sound of your own.
Deleting the Title Sounds bar turns that title's Sounds off rather than putting it back.
The track the bar lands on is named Audio 2 (the next free audio name), not after the title.

The sounds are made by the app, not recorded: a band-swept noise whoosh and a two-tone tick. I could not listen to them on this machine during an unmanned run; they are checked by their shape (swell, short tick, peak 14 dB under full scale) and by the exported file's levels lining up with the build.
Big accents (Light Leak's washes, a glass panel) do not tick on purpose; Tech Terminal's typing gets a whoosh, not a keystroke per letter.
